speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any specific patterns to the rash, such as it worsening at night or spreading after physical activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Has she experienced joint pain, swollen lymph nodes, or any mucosal changes like a rash inside her mouth or on her eyes?

Also, did anyone around her have a similar rash or recent viral illness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Fifth Disease (Erythema Infectiosum) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The classic "slapped cheek" facial rash combined with a subsequent lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, following a viral prodrome of fever, headache, and rhinorrhea, is highly characteristic of this condition. No further testing is required as the diagnosis is clinical.
